works.title: Selective Hydrogen Transport Through Polymeric Fullerene Nanosheet Membranes
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Lamellar membranes, assembled from two‐dimensional (2D) nanosheets, have attracted intensive attention for molecular and ion sieving due to their tunable interlayer channels and ultrathin selective layers. However, molecular transport in conventional lamellar membranes usually occurs through interlayer galleries whose dimensions vary with stacking, limiting ångström‐scale control over selectivity. Therefore, developing a novel lamellar membrane with ångström‐scale in‐plane pores is highly desirable. In an idealized qTP lattice, four‐directionally connected fullerene cages define periodically distributed apertures that converge from an approximately 5.87 Å entrance to a 3.11 Å waist. Upon assembly, the constriction regions can discriminate by size, while their converging entrances and the intersheet galleries govern molecular access and transport resistance through the in‐plane apertures. The resulting polymeric fullerene nanosheet membrane exhibits an H 2 permeance of 3896 ± 107 GPU and an H 2 /CO 2 separation factor of 88.5 ± 5.9 for the separation of an equimolar H 2 /CO 2 mixture at 303.15 K and a total feed pressure of 100 kPa. The separation performance remains stable over 200 h of operation. This study establishes topology‐encoded pore geometry as a design principle for integrating short selective pathways with ångström‐scale molecular discrimination in lamellar membranes.

works.title: High-flux dual-charged composite nanofiltration membranes with electrical double layer architectures for efficient low-pressure water purification
works.journal: Frontiers in Membrane Science and Technology
institutions: Zhejiang Mey Membrane Technology Co.,Ltd, Xindeng
works.abstract: Traditional thin-film composite (TFC) nanofiltration (NF) membranes are constrained by a permeability–selectivity trade-off arising from limited surface charge density and high hydraulic resistance contributed by non-woven fabric backing layers. Here we report high-flux composite Nanofiltration membranes engineered with a dual electrical double layer (EDL) architecture that integrates charged functional groups into both the porous support and the ultrathin selective layer. Strongly negatively charged membranes based on sulfonated polyvinylidene fluoride or sulfonated polyethersulfone achieved multivalent salt rejections of 95.6%–99.3% while delivering pure-water permeances up to approximately 37 L m -2 h -1 bar -1 . Non-woven-free variants maintained stable, high-efficiency removal of multivalent salts, heavy-metal ions (Pb 2+ ), viruses, and bacteria under ultra-low operating pressures (≤0.1 MPa). Zeta-potential measurements confirmed that the dual-charged EDL structures sustain high-magnitude, pH-invariant surface potentials across the range pH 1–13. These membranes enable pump-free household filtration, municipal water treatment, wastewater reclamation, and decentralized rural water supply, directly addressing the need for energy-efficient, high-selectivity water purification technologies.

works.title: Two-Dimensional Membranes for High-Value Ion Separation from Seawater and Brines
institutions: Tianjin Municipal Engineering Design and Research Institute
works.abstract: Seawater and brines contain substantial inventories of high-value ions, yet their extraction is constrained by dilute targets, concentrated competitors and feed-dependent speciation. Two-dimensional (2D) membranes offer short, tunable pathways that can amplify subtle differences in ion size, hydration, charge, and coordination. This review integrates ionic properties and aqueous speciation with membrane structure to establish a mechanistic framework for ion selectivity in 2D nanochannels. It critically examines size exclusion, dehydration, electrostatic partitioning, chemical recognition, and coupled non-ideal transport and evaluates their relevance to Li, U, Cs, Sr, Rb, and other underexplored ions. Major membrane platforms, including graphene-based materials, MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides, 2D metal–organic and covalent organic frameworks, layered inorganic materials and heterolamellar composites, are compared in terms of channel architecture, chemical tunability, stability, and manufacturability. The available evidence indicates that selectivity is not an intrinsic property of a nominal pore or material class, but an operating-state response of the coupled ion–solvent–membrane–electrolyte system. Finally, this review critically examines rational membrane-design strategies, outstanding challenges and future research priorities to guide the development of high-performance 2D membranes for the selective separation of high-value ions.

works.title: ЯВИЩЕ КОНЦЕНТРАЦІЙНОЇ ПОЛЯРИЗАЦІЇ: СТАН ПРОБЛЕМИІ АКТУАЛЬНІ НАПРЯМКИ ДОСЛІДЖЕНЬ
institutions: National Technical University of Ukraine “Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute”
works.abstract: Concentration polarization is one of the key mass transfer phenomena occurring in membrane separation processes, electrochemical systems, heat and mass transfer equipment, and numerous technological processes in power engineering and industrial machinery. The phenomenon is associated with the formation of a concentration boundary layer near the phase interface, where the concentration of dissolved substances differs significantly from that in the bulk solution. This results in additional diffusion resistance, reduced process productivity, increased energy consumption, accelerated membrane fouling, and shortened equipment service life. As the requirements for energy efficiency, operational reliability, and environmental sustainability continue to increase, concentration polarization has become one of the major challenges limiting the performance of modern membrane and mass transfer systems. The aim of this study is to summarize the current state of research on concentration polarization in membrane-based water treatment and desalination processes, to analyze the physical mechanisms responsible for its formation, to review contemporary theoretical, numerical, and experimental approaches to its investigation, and to identify promising directions for minimizing its adverse effects. The study is based on a comprehensive analysis and systematization of recent scientific publications devoted to reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, and forward osmosis technologies. Particular attention is given to modern mathematical models describing concentration polarization, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, and advanced experimental techniques, including digital holographic interferometry and laser-induced fluorescence, which enable direct visualization of concentration boundary layers and local mass transfer phenomena. The influence of membrane structure, channel geometry, hydrodynamic conditions, flow turbulators, and membrane surface properties on the development of concentration polarization is analyzed. Special consideration is also given to internal concentration polarization in forward osmosis membranes and to recent advances in nanocomposite membrane materials designed to reduce concentration polarization and membrane fouling. The review demonstrates that integrating experimental observations with numerical simulations provides new opportunities for understanding and controlling concentration polarization in complex engineering systems. Furthermore, the rapid development of digital twins, artificial intelligence, and machine learning technologies creates new possibilities for predictive modeling, process optimization, and intelligent control of membrane systems. The practical significance of the study lies in the systematization of modern approaches aimed at mitigating concentration polarization and membrane fouling, the results of which can be applied in the design, optimization, and operation of membrane equipment for water treatment, desalination, and other industrial mass transfer processes.

works.title: Integrated UF–NF–RO treatment of vinasse for nutrient recovery and multicriteria assessment of agricultural and off-site water reuse
authors: Lauro Shikazu Alvares Da Silva Toma
works.abstract: This study evaluated an integrated ultrafiltration–nanofiltration–reverse osmosis (UF–NF–RO) route to fractionate vinasse into nutrient-rich concentrates and water for different reuse applications. Five NF and two RO membranes were compared regarding permeate flux, fouling, solute rejection, specific energy consumption, operational cost, and membrane-surface changes. The retentates were further ranked for fertigation and the permeates for off-site applications using AHP, TOPSIS, and VIKOR. UF removed 99.6% of turbidity and 85.1% of color while allowing most dissolved nitrogen and potassium to remain in the permeate, supporting downstream nutrient concentration. Cake fouling and intermediate pore blocking predominated during UF. Among NF membranes, Duracid provided the highest flux and lowest specific energy consumption but limited ion retention. NF90 offered the best performance balance, with removals of 86.1% NH₃, 87.0% phosphate, 87.8% potassium, and 87.5% sodium, combined with low energy demand and limited membrane fouling. In the RO stage, BW30 achieved removals of 90.1% COD, 99.3% color, 92.1% electrical conductivity, and 93.8% potassium, producing the highest-quality permeate, although at greater energy and operational costs. The multicriteria analysis identified the UF–NF270-RO(BW30) route as the preferred option for resource recovery, and UF-NF90-RO(BW30) if external reuse is preferred. By integrating nutrient recovery with fit-for-purpose water production and accounting for energy and economic performance, this approach provides an application-oriented pathway toward more sustainable resource management within the water cycle.

works.title: Ion Valence Difference Governs Membrane Charge Preference in Nanofiltration-Based Radionuclide Separation
works.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of radionuclides with varying environmental hazards is critical for mitigating the disposal burden of high-level radioactive wastewater. Although positively charged (PC) membranes are generally considered effective for cation pair separation, the applicability of negatively charged (NC) membranes for separating cations with large valence differences remains unresolved. In this study, Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ were used as representative radionuclides with large and small valence differences, respectively, to evaluate the separation performance and underlying mechanisms of PC and NC membranes. Notably, NC membranes maintained near-complete rejection of Zr4+ while simultaneously exhibiting higher Ag+ permeability, thereby achieving superior Ag+/Zr4+ selectivity relative to PC membranes. DFT calculations and MD simulations revealed that strong ion–membrane interactions facilitated preferential partitioning of Zr4+ at the NC membrane interface, whereas differences in hydration energy governed the competitive transport of Ag+ and Zr4+. Furthermore, Zr4+ accumulated at the membrane surface induced incomplete dehydration of Ag+, reducing interfacial transport barriers and promoting Ag+ permeation. Comparative analysis of Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ systems further demonstrated that ion valence difference governs the preference of membrane charges: NC membranes are preferred for M+/M4+ separations, whereas PC membranes are preferred for M+/M2+ separations, which was further validated by Li+/Mg2+ and Li+/Ti4+ separations. These findings clarify the mechanistic distinction between co-ion and counterion competition, providing guidance for the selection of membrane charge types for energy-efficient radionuclide separation and selective resource recovery beyond the nuclear industry.

works.title: Preferential Transport of Mg2+ over Li+ in Negatively Charged Styrene Sulfonate-Regulated Graphene Oxide Nanochannels
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient lithium recovery from salt-lake brines is severely hindered by their high Mg2+/Li+ ratios. Recent nanofiltration technologies primarily directly extract lithium from brine, which incurs high energy consumption. Herein, using pressure-driven molecular dynamics simulations at 5 MPa (representative of practical operating pressures), we propose a strategy for preferential Mg2+ transport over Li+ to lower the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratios for further low-energy lithium extraction, based on intercalating styrene sulfonate inside graphene oxide nanochannels (SS–@GO). The results demonstrate a reversal in permeation selectivity from Li+ to Mg2+ upon negatively charging the lamellar channel through SS– insertion at an interlayer spacing of 1.8 nm (d). The Mg2+/Li+ selectivity exhibited a nonmonotonic dependence on negative charge density, first increasing and then decreasing, with the highest selectivity obtained at ρ = −2.07 × 10–3 e/Å2. The Mg2+/Li+ separation factor of the SS–@GO membrane can reach 16.4 at an Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio of 35. Notably, we observe that not all ions entering the channel successfully permeate, and some are reflected back to the feed side, particularly at higher negative charge densities. These findings provide molecular guidance for designing Mg2+-selective GO membrane to pretreat brines with high Mg2+/Li+ mass ratios prior to lithium recovery.

works.title: Non-Monotonic Dependence of Ion Selectivity on Interfacial Polymerization Time in Nanofiltration Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Polyamide nanofiltration (NF) membranes offer promising opportunities for resource recovery because their sub-nanometer selective layers provide intrinsic ion−ion selectivity. However, achieving sufficient monovalent/divalent separation, such as Li+/Mg2+, remains challenging because the polyamide (PA) structure formed during interfacial polymerization (IP) is heterogeneous and difficult to control. As a time-dependent process, IP enables reaction time to regulate the PA layer structure and ion transport. Here, we systematically investigate IP reaction times from 10 s to 5 min in polyamide NF membranes and show that monovalent/divalent ion selectivity exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the reaction time, reaching a maximum separation factor of 30.5 at 0.5 min. Shorter reaction times increased water permeance and reduced ion rejection due to incomplete polymerization, whereas prolonged reaction decreased water permeance and MgCl2 rejection while increasing LiCl rejection. Membrane characterization revealed that these trends arise from coupled changes in the PA network density and charge distribution. The 0.5 min reaction produced a thin (32 nm) and densely cross-linked PA, favoring water transport and steric exclusion of Mg2+. In contrast, the 5 min reaction produced a substantially thicker (117 nm) and more open PA layer containing carboxylic groups throughout its depth, contributing to stronger electrostatic exclusion of LiCl. These findings establish the IP reaction time as an important parameter for tuning the structure and charge of PA membranes, enabling improved control of monovalent/divalent ion selectivity.

works.title: Organic Solvent Nanofiltration Properties of Silica-based Membranes Derived from Propyltrimethoxysilane and Bis(triethoxysilyl)ethane
works.journal: Journal of the Japan Petroleum Institute
institutions: Dept. of Chemical, Energy and Environmental Engineering, Kansai University
works.abstract: Membranes with a molecular weight cutoff of approximately 300 Da are very useful for organic solvent nanofiltration applications in the pharmaceutical industry, especially for recovery of active pharmaceutical ingredients. However, achieving such molecular weight cutoff values using polymeric membranes is challenging because most polymeric materials swell or deteriorate in organic solvents. In this study, we prepared propyl-functionalized silica (PrFS) membranes using propyltrimethoxysilane (PrTMS) and bis(triethoxysilyl)ethane (BTESE) as silica precursors. Compared with conventional templated PrFS membranes, the PrTMS–BTESE membranes exhibited higher organic solvent permeance with a high methyl orange (molecular weight: 327 Da) rejection, and did not require template removal. The membranes demonstrated excellent performance in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone, with a permeance of up to 0.20 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 and a rejection of 89-99 % for methyl orange. Thermal treatment was critical in optimizing the membrane pore size, hydrophobicity, and separation performance. These findings highlight the potential of PrTMS–BTESE membranes for organic solvent nanofiltration. The membranes can have finely optimized properties for solvent-stable separation in pharmaceutical and chemical processes.

works.title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

works.title: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
works.abstract: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.

works.title: Influence of nanoscale effects and gradient pore-structure characteristics on the permeability of nanofiltration membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Understanding the coupled influence of nanoscale interfacial effects and pore structure is essential for clarifying water-transport mechanisms in nanofiltration (NF) membranes. Previous studies have mainly examined either nanoscale transport effects, such as wall slip and interfacial viscosity variation, or membrane structural parameters independently, while their combined effects on membrane permeability remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, physical models of inhomogeneous, homogeneous, and gradient membrane structures were constructed, and nanopore-scale water transport was simulated using the lattice Boltzmann method while accounting for wettability-dependent slip and interfacial viscosity. The results show that, compared with the no-slip condition, nanoscale interfacial effects suppress water transport in hydrophilic membranes but substantially enhance it in hydrophobic membranes, and their influence becomes stronger as the pore size decreases. In addition, pore-size uniformity, porosity, specific interface, and membrane thickness significantly affect permeability. A characteristic factor incorporating porosity, specific interface, and thickness was proposed to describe the permeability of gradient membranes, with smaller values corresponding to higher permeability. Structural variations exert a stronger influence on hydrophobic membranes because nanoscale interfacial effects amplify the response of water transport to pore-structure changes. These results clarify the coupled roles of nanoscale interfacial transport and pore structure in NF membrane permeability and provide a physical basis for the coordinated optimization of membrane structure and interfacial properties.

works.title: Vapor Phase Infiltration of Metal Oxides for Water Treatment Membranes: Potential and Limitations
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane-based water treatment processes are critical for global water security, yet current state-of-the-art polymeric membranes face limitations in mechanical, chemical, and thermal stability. Ceramic membranes, on the other hand, foul less, are easy to clean, and have high modulus values, but they are brittle and less permeable when used as dense membranes. Vapor phase infiltration (VPI) of metal oxides, a derivative of atomic layer deposition (ALD) that transforms organic polymers into organic–inorganic hybrid materials, offers a novel method to modify polymeric membranes and allow them to have the advantages of both polymeric and ceramic membranes. In this review, we combine insights from the use of VPI with polymeric substrates and organic solvent separation membranes to provide our view of the potential and limitations of VPI for enhancing water treatment membranes. We examine how VPI of metal oxides improves the mechanical strength, which is relevant to compaction-resistant reverse osmosis supports, and chemical stability, which could play a role in membrane chlorine and extreme-pH tolerance. We also critically evaluate the associated trade-offs, most notably potential reductions in water permeance arising from the intrinsically lower water permeability of metal oxides. We further identify ion exchange membranes and electrodialysis as especially promising targets, where suppressed water transport is advantageous for ion–ion selectivity. Together, these insights clarify where VPI of metal oxides can most effectively advance emerging membrane-based water treatment technologies.

works.title: pH-gated ion transport in covalent organic framework membranes functionalized with oxygen-containing groups
works.abstract: Covalent organic framework (COF) membranes with pH-gated ion transport hold promise for smart nanofluidic devices, yet the regulatory mechanisms of different oxygen-containing functional groups remain poorly understood. Herein, we systematically investigate the pH-dependent ionic conductance of TpPa-R COF membranes (R = -SO<sub>3</sub>H, -COOH, -OH) across pH 3 to 11.5 using unmodified TpPa as a reference. All membranes exhibit nanofluidic transport with a U-shaped conductance profile as a function of pH. The neutral-pH conductance is governed by the effective surface charge density that drives counterion enrichment. Among the three modifications, the TpPa-SO<sub>3</sub>H membrane displays the broadest pH response and the highest conductance at both acidic and alkaline extremes. Notably, the TpPa-COOH membrane shows unexpectedly lower conductance than TpPa-OH at pH ≥ 5, which we attribute to hydration screening that reduces the effective charge of the carboxylate groups, whereas deprotonation of the phenol groups in TpPa-OH enhances effective surface charge density and conductance at high pH. All membranes demonstrate reversible pH-switching over the tested range. This work provides a molecular-level design rationale for tailoring pH-gating performance in COF membranes and a foundation for developing tunable ion-transport devices with predictable pH responsiveness.

works.title: A Sustainable, Robust, Soft‐Gated Janus Bio‐Membrane for High‐Flux Aromatic Recovery From Saline Industrial Wastewaters
works.abstract: ABSTRACT The selective recovery of aromatic pollutants from saline wastewater remains a central challenge in sustainable chemical engineering. We present a bio‐derived Janus membrane that couples a sorption‐active, mechanically robust wood scaffold with an ultrathin polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer for soft‐gated aromatic transport. Spectroscopic, molecular, and free‐volume analyses support transient hydroxyl‐mediated phenol capture, favorable interfacial association, and onward diffusion through PDMS. The membrane achieves an overall phenol mass‐transfer coefficient of 36.9 × 10 −7 m s −1 and 99.4% salt rejection under ambient conditions, with sustained performance in petrochemical and offshore oilfield wastewaters. It combines a tensile strength of ∼70 MPa with consistent separation performance across a meter‐long sheet. Life‐cycle and national‐scale analyses indicate over 85% reductions in environmental impact and over 42 000 tons of CO 2 ‐equivalent mitigation annually. This work establishes a scalable bio‐derived membrane architecture that bridges molecular transport design with aromatic resource recovery, advancing the valorization of saline industrial wastewaters.

works.title: Digital-Assisted Workflow for Organic Solvent Nanofiltration: Accelerating Process Development in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
works.abstract: Abstract Organic solvents contribute more than 80% of total process mass intensity (PMI) in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Although organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) diafiltration processes can improve sustainability, achieving high product yield typically requires large solvent volume to operate. Here, we present a digital-assisted workflow, built on the OSN Designer framework, that enables rapid screening of OSN process configurations to identify architectures that minimize solvent consumption while maintaining API recovery. The framework integrates a solution-diffusion transport model, film theory for concentration polarization, and non-steady-state mass balances, calibrated from crossflow experiments with compound A on the Borsig oNF-3 membrane in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran. Validated with average concordance correlation coefficient (ccc) of 0.72 across steady-state and dynamic operating regimes, the model was applied without recalibration to evaluate four process configurations. A two-stage membrane cascade with closed-loop permeate recycling achieved a process mass intensity (PMI) of 7.76─a 92.4% reduction relative to the single-stage constant-volume diafiltration baseline (PMI 101.5). The formalized four-phase workflow reduces experimental effort to approximately 3 weeks from more than 6–8 months and is directly transferable to other pharmaceutical OSN systems.

works.title: Highly Interconnected Cellulose Acetate Ultrafiltration Membranes via Interfacial Hydration-Induced Phase Separation for Ultrafast Water Purification
works.abstract: Abstract Ultrafiltration is essential for ensuring water security, yet commercial ultrafiltration membranes remain constrained by the permeability-selectivity trade-off. While extensive research has focused on designing the selective skin layer, such improvements in permeance have neared a bottleneck due to the often-overlooked hydraulic resistance arising from the underlying sponge-like layer. Here, we propose a generalizable interfacial hydration-induced phase separation strategy to reconstruct the internal transport channels within the sponge-like layer of biodegradable cellulose acetate (CA) ultrafiltration membranes, enhancing permeance without sacrificing selectivity. Specifically, highly polar nanoclusters (TCZ), formed in situ via multidentate coordination between tannic acid-modified cellulose nanocrystals (TC) and Zr4+ ions, preferentially anchor within the sponge-like layer through strong interfacial interactions with the CA matrix. Acting as localized hydration seeds, these nanoclusters attract and enrich water molecules to establish water-rich microenvironments through strong hydrogen-bonding interactions, promoting local liquid–liquid demixing and driving the formation of highly interconnected, low-tortuosity water-transport pathways throughout the sponge-like layer. The resulting CTCZ membranes exhibit high water permeance (752.29 L m–2 h–1 bar–1), representing a 10-fold increase over the CA membrane, with high rejection (>96%) for typical water contaminants. Notably, this strategy can also be extended to mainstream polyvinylidene fluoride and poly(ether sulfone) matrices, yielding 13-fold and 21-fold permeance enhancements, respectively. Large-area NW-CTCZ membranes fabricated via a roll-to-roll process demonstrate reliable long-term stability in surface water purification. Furthermore, life-cycle and economic analyses confirm that the CTCZ membranes, as eco-friendly and cost-effective candidates, offer a scalable and sustainable approach for water treatment.

works.title: Redirecting gypsum scaling in pervaporation desalination via activated alumina granules
works.abstract: Membrane scaling, particularly CaSO4 (gypsum) crystallisation, severely limits the practical application of pervaporation (PV) desalination for high-salinity wastewater treatment. Herein, an online interception strategy using nitric acid-activated alumina granules (AAG) is proposed to redirect gypsum scaling from the membrane surface to a sacrificial medium. By tuning nitric acid activation, the physicochemical properties of AAG were optimised. AAG activated with 7.5% nitric acid exhibits an optimal pore structure (specific surface area of 295.4 m2/g, pore volume of 0.361 cm3/g) and surface positive charge, significantly reducing the heterogeneous nucleation energy barrier for gypsum crystallisation. This enables the transfer of scaling from the membrane surface to AAG, reducing the membrane surface scaling amount by approximately 45%. Combined with the extended XDLVO theory analysis, the dominant mechanism of surface-induced heterogeneous nucleation by AAG was elucidated. Moreover, ultrasonic–EDTA cleaning enables efficient regeneration of AAG, and the strategy is validated using real reverse osmosis concentrate. This work establishes a scaling control paradigm based on crystallisation relocation rather than inhibition, providing mechanistic insight and a scalable approach for fouling mitigation in PV desalination.
